questions.question: Which of the following is a major factor that has facilitated globalisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rapid improvements in technology**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Technological advancements have significantly lowered transportation and communication costs, making global trade more efficient and accessible.
 
• The internet and digital technologies have facilitated instant communication and data exchange across the globe, enhancing international business operations.
 
• Improvements in shipping and logistics technology have reduced the time and cost of moving goods across borders, boosting international trade.
 
• Advances in information technology have enabled companies to manage global supply chains more effectively, coordinating production and distribution worldwide.
 
• Technological innovation has also led to the development of new products and services, opening up new markets and driving economic globalization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Supply Chains:** Technological advancements have enabled the development of complex global supply chains, where production processes are distributed across multiple countries to optimize costs and efficiency.
 
• **Telecommunications:** The evolution of telecommunications, including mobile networks and internet connectivity, has facilitated real-time communication and collaboration between businesses and individuals worldwide.
 
• **E-commerce:** The rise of e-commerce platforms has allowed businesses to reach international customers directly, bypassing traditional physical retail channels and expanding their global presence.
 
• **Automation and Robotics:** Technological innovations in automation and robotics have increased productivity and efficiency in manufacturing, enabling companies to compete globally by reducing production costs.
 
• **Financial Technologies:** Developments in financial technologies (FinTech) have streamlined international payments and transactions, making it easier for businesses to operate across borders.

questions.question: Who is the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu as of September 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**MK Stalin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **MK Stalin** is the current Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu.
 
• He assumed office on **May 7, 2021**.
 
• He is the leader of the **Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK)** party.
 
• MK Stalin is the son of former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, **M. Karunanidhi**.
 
• Under his leadership, the DMK won a decisive victory in the **2021 Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly elections**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK)**

 
 
• Founded in 1949 by **C. N. Annadurai**.
 
• It is a prominent political party in the state of Tamil Nadu and has a strong presence in neighboring **Puducherry**.
 
• The party's symbol is the **rising sun**.
 
• DMK has a legacy of promoting **Dravidian and social justice ideologies**.
 
 
 
• **M. Karunanidhi**
 
 
• Served as the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu for five terms.
 
• He was a key figure in the Dravidian movement and contributed significantly to Tamil literature and cinema.
 
• Karunanidhi was also known for his contributions to social justice and economic development in Tamil Nadu.
 
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly**
 
 
• The legislative body of the state of Tamil Nadu.
 
• It consists of **234 elected members**.
 
• Assembly elections are held every five years.
 
• The majority party or coalition forms the government, and its leader becomes the Chief Minister.
 
 
 
• **2021 Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly Elections**
 
 
• Held in a single phase on April 6, 2021.
 
• The DMK-led alliance won a **majority** with 159 seats.
 
• The AIADMK-led alliance won 75 seats.
 
• These elections marked the return of DMK to power after a decade.

questions.question: Who was the first President of the All India Muslim League, founded in 1906?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aga Khan III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Aga Khan III** was the first President of the All India Muslim League, which was founded in 1906.
 
• The All India Muslim League was established to advocate for the rights of Muslims in British India.
 
• Aga Khan III played a crucial role in the formation and leadership of the league, guiding its initial steps and objectives.
 
• His leadership was significant in shaping the political landscape for Muslims in India during the early 20th century.
 
• The league later became a driving force behind the creation of Pakistan in 1947.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **All India Muslim League**:

 
 
• Founded on 30 December 1906 at Dacca (now Dhaka), it was the political party representing the interests of the Muslim population in British India.
 
• The league's formation was in response to the growing need for a separate political platform for Muslims to safeguard their rights and interests.
 
• Key figures included Sir Sultan Muhammad Shah (Aga Khan III), Nawab Salimullah, and others.
 
 
 
• **Aga Khan III**:
 
 
• Born as Sir Sultan Mahomed Shah, he was the 48th Imam of the Nizari Ismaili Muslims.
 
• He was a prominent leader and philanthropist, significantly contributing to education and healthcare for Muslims.
 
• He also played an influential role in the international Muslim community through organizations like the League of Nations.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Pakistan Movement**:
 
 
• The All India Muslim League was instrumental in the demand for a separate Muslim state, leading to the creation of Pakistan in 1947.
 
• Under the leadership of Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the league's demand for Pakistan became a reality.
 
• The Lahore Resolution of 1940, passed by the league, was a turning point in the Pakistan Movement.
 
 
 
• **Legacy**:
 
 
• The All India Muslim League's legacy continues in Pakistan, where it laid the foundation for the nation's political framework.
 
• It inspired subsequent political movements and parties in both Pakistan and India.
 
• The contributions of early leaders like Aga Khan III are remembered for their vision and efforts towards Muslim empowerment.

questions.question: Who was conferred a gold medal in 1968 by the Mexican government for her choreography?

• Mrinalini Sarabhai was the founder of the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in Ahmedabad, India.
 
• She was trained in Bharatanatyam, Kathakali, and Mohiniyattam, which she often incorporated into her choreographic works.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• A major form of Indian classical dance that originated in Tamil Nadu.

• **Darpana Academy of Performing Arts**
 
 
• Founded by Mrinalini Sarabhai in 1949 in Ahmedabad.

questions.question: Name the virus spread by mosquitoes that causes inflammation in the brain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Japanese encephalitis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Japanese encephalitis (JE) is a viral infection that causes inflammation of the brain.
 
• The virus is transmitted by the bite of infected mosquitoes, primarily the Culex species.
 
• JE is prevalent in rural and agricultural areas of Asia and the Western Pacific.
 
• Symptoms of JE include high fever, headache, neck stiffness, disorientation, coma, seizures, and paralysis.
 
• There is no specific antiviral treatment for JE; supportive care is the primary approach.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transmission Cycle**

 
 
• The JE virus is maintained in a cycle involving mosquitoes and vertebrate hosts, primarily pigs and wading birds.
 
• Humans are incidental hosts and do not contribute to the transmission cycle.
 
 
 
• **Vaccination**
 
 
• Vaccination is the most effective way to prevent JE.
 
• Several types of JE vaccines are available, including inactivated and live-attenuated vaccines.
 
 
 
• **Prevention**
 
 
• Preventive measures include using mosquito nets, insect repellents, and wearing protective clothing.
 
• Control of mosquito populations through environmental management and insecticide use is crucial.
 
 
 
• **Global Impact**
 
 
• JE is a significant public health issue in many Asian countries, with thousands of cases reported annually.
 
• Outbreaks often occur in regions with endemic JE and can lead to high morbidity and mortality rates.

questions.question: As per Census 2011, which of the following streams of migration has the highest percentage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rural to rural**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per Census 2011, the most common type of internal migration in India is from **rural areas to other rural areas**.
 
• This type of migration accounts for about **47.4%** of the total internal migration.
 
• One of the major reasons for rural to rural migration is **marriage**, especially among women.
 
• Another reason is the movement of **agricultural laborers** in search of work.
 
• Rural to rural migration is also driven by **seasonal work** in agriculture and related sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census 2011 Migration Data**

 
 
• The Census of India 2011 provides detailed data on migration patterns within the country.
 
• It categorizes migration into four streams: rural to rural, rural to urban, urban to urban, and urban to rural.
 
• Understanding these patterns helps in planning and policy formulation for regional development.
 
 
 
• **Types of Migration**
 
 
• **Internal Migration:** Movement within a country, such as from one state or region to another.
 
• **External Migration:** Movement across country boundaries, also known as international migration.
 
 
 
• **Reasons for Migration**
 
 
• **Economic:** Search for better employment opportunities and living conditions.
 
• **Social:** Marriage, family reunification, and education.
 
• **Environmental:** Natural disasters, climate change, and environmental degradation.
 
• **Political:** Conflict, persecution, and instability.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Migration**
 
 
• Can lead to **urbanization** and growth of cities.
 
• May cause **strain on urban infrastructure** and resources.
 
• Contributes to **cultural exchange** and diversity.
 
• Can result in **brain drain** or **skill shortages** in the areas of origin.

questions.question: For a book of mass m, moving a distance d on a smooth horizontal table, the work done due gravitational force is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The work done by a force is defined as the dot product of the force and the displacement in the direction of the force.
 
• On a smooth horizontal table, the gravitational force acts vertically downward, while the displacement is horizontal.
 
• The angle between the gravitational force and the horizontal displacement is 90 degrees.
 
• The cosine of 90 degrees is 0, hence the work done by the gravitational force over the horizontal displacement is zero.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Work**: In physics, work is done when a force acts upon an object to cause a displacement. It is calculated as the product of the force and the displacement in the direction of the force.
 
• **Gravitational Force**: The force of attraction between two masses. Near the Earth's surface, it imparts an acceleration of 9.81 m/s² downward.
 
• **Dot Product**: A mathematical operation that takes two equal-length sequences of numbers (usually coordinate vectors) and returns a single number. It is defined as the product of the magnitudes of the two vectors and the cosine of the angle between them.
 
• **Cosine Function**: In trigonometry, the cosine of an angle in a right-angled triangle is the ratio of the length of the adjacent side to the length of the hypotenuse. The cosine of 90 degrees is 0.
 
• **Smooth Surface**: A surface with no friction. On a smooth horizontal table, there is no resistance to horizontal motion, and thus gravitational force does not affect horizontal displacement.

questions.question: Who among the following was appointed as the Minister of Tribal Affairs in June 2024?

The correct answer is __**Jual Oram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The ministry implements various schemes for education, health, economic development, and social empowerment of tribal populations.
 
 
 
• **Jual Oram's Background**

• He has been actively involved in various developmental projects aimed at improving the living standards of tribal people.
 
 
 
• **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**
 
 
• The BJP is one of the two major political parties in India, along with the Indian National Congress (INC).

questions.question: Ali-Aye-Ligang, the spring festival, is observed on the first Wednesday of the Phagun month in the Indian state of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ali-Aye-Ligang is a significant spring festival celebrated by the Mising community in Assam.
 
• The festival marks the beginning of the sowing season and is held on the first Wednesday of the Phagun month (February-March).
 
• The name "Ali-Aye-Ligang" translates to "sowing of seeds" in the Mising language.
 
• During the festival, traditional dances, music, and feasts are organized to celebrate the agricultural cycle.
 
• It is an important cultural event that emphasizes the agrarian lifestyle and traditions of the Mising tribe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mising Tribe**

 
 
• The Mising are one of the largest ethnic groups in Assam.
 
• They are primarily agrarian and have a rich cultural heritage with distinct traditions and rituals.
 
• Their traditional attire includes the "Mekhela Sador" for women and "Dhoti" and "Gamosa" for men.
 
 
 
• **Phagun Month**
 
 
• Phagun is the twelfth month of the Hindu calendar, corresponding to February-March in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• It marks the end of winter and the beginning of the spring season.
 
• Several Indian festivals, including Holi, are celebrated during this month.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Festivals in India**
 
 
• India, being an agrarian country, celebrates various agricultural festivals such as Baisakhi, Pongal, and Makar Sankranti.
 
• These festivals are region-specific and mark important phases in the agricultural cycle.
 
• They often involve rituals, dances, and community feasts to invoke blessings for a good harvest.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Dances of Assam**
 
 
• Assam has a rich tradition of folk dances, including Bihu, Bagurumba, and Sattriya.
 
• Bihu dance is performed during the Bihu festival, celebrating the Assamese New Year and the farming season.
 
• Sattriya is a classical dance form that originated from the Vaishnavite monasteries of Assam.

questions.question: Which of the following does not come under the power of the Governor of a State in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Obligatory power**__ .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Constitution of India, the Governor has executive, legislative and judicial powers.
 
• The executive power helps the Governor in performing the functions of the state government.
 
• The Governor can exercise discretionary power independently under special circumstances.
 
• Under the legislative power, the Governor can convene meetings of the legislature and issue ordinances.
 
• Compulsory power is not included in the powers of the Governor, as no such power has been given in the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Executive Power:** The Governor is the head of the state executive and acts on the advice of the State Council of Ministers.
 
• **Legislative Power:** The Governor has the power to convene, adjourn and dissolve the Assembly.
 
• **Discretionary Power:** The Governor can take decisions independently without the advice of the State Council of Ministers in certain matters.
 
• **Judicial Power:** The Governor has the power to decide on mercy petitions.
 
• **Constitutional Power:** The Governor takes an oath to protect and preserve the Constitution and ensure that it is followed in the state.

questions.question: Which musical instrument is played by Yella Venkateswara Rao, an Indian classical musician and percussionist?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mridangam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Yella Venkateswara Rao is an eminent Indian classical musician and percussionist specializing in the **Mridangam**.
 
• He is renowned for his exceptional skills and contributions to the art of Mridangam playing.
 
• Yella Venkateswara Rao has performed in numerous prestigious concerts and festivals both in India and abroad.
 
• He has been honored with several awards and titles, recognizing his mastery and dedication to Indian classical music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mridangam:**

 
 
• A double-sided drum used in Carnatic music, the classical music of South India.
 
• It is made of a hollowed-out piece of jackfruit wood and covered with goat skin on both sides.
 
• The right side produces higher-pitched sounds, while the left side produces bass tones.
 
• The Mridangam is considered the principal percussion instrument in South Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music:**
 
 
• A system of music commonly associated with the southern part of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It is one of the two main sub-genres of Indian classical music, the other being Hindustani music.
 
• Carnatic music emphasizes vocal music and is characterized by a rich tradition of compositions and improvisations.
 
 
 
• **Yella Venkateswara Rao's Contributions:**
 
 
• He has significantly contributed to the popularization and teaching of Mridangam.
 
• His innovative techniques and performances have inspired many young musicians.
 
 
 
• **Recognition and Awards:**
 
 
• Yella Venkateswara Rao has received numerous accolades, including the prestigious Padma Shri award.
 
• He is also known for his philanthropic efforts in promoting music education.

questions.question: Which Five-Year Plan aimed to achieve self-reliance and aimed at 'growth with stability'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fourth Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974)** aimed to achieve **self-reliance** and emphasized **growth with stability** in India’s economy.
 
• This plan focused on **increased industrial production** and **reducing dependence on foreign imports** by encouraging domestic production.
 
• It aimed to strengthen the agriculture sector while promoting technological advancements, particularly in heavy industries and infrastructure.
 
• The goal was to enhance the overall economic structure, reduce poverty, and improve social and industrial development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Fourth Plan was introduced under the leadership of Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**, during a period of political instability and a focus on strengthening national unity.
 
• **Self-reliance** was a key theme, as India sought to reduce its dependence on foreign aid and promote indigenous growth in sectors such as agriculture, manufacturing, and defense.
 
• The Fourth Plan also saw efforts in the **Green Revolution**, aimed at increasing agricultural productivity, especially in staple crops like wheat and rice.
 
• Despite these efforts, the plan faced challenges like the **Indo-Pakistani War of 1971** and an energy crisis that hindered its full success.
 
• The focus on growth with stability continued in subsequent plans, but the Fourth Plan marked a crucial step in India’s journey toward economic self-sufficiency.
 
• Subsequent Five-Year Plans shifted focus, such as the **Sixth Plan** (1980-1985), which prioritized poverty alleviation and employment generation.

questions.question: Under which amendment of the Constitution of India was Right to Property removed from the list of Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**44th Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights.
 
• The Right to Property was originally provided under Article 31 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• After the amendment, the Right to Property was made a legal right under Article 300A.
 
• This amendment was introduced to curb the misuse of the right and to facilitate land reforms.
 
• The amendment aimed to balance individual rights and the need for socio-economic justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights**

 
 
• These are a set of rights that are recognized under the Indian Constitution as being essential for the all-round development of individuals.
 
• The Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution.
 
• They include rights such as the right to equality, freedom of speech, and protection against discrimination.
 
• These rights are enforceable by the courts, subject to certain restrictions.
 
 
 
• **Article 31**
 
 
• Before the 44th Amendment, Article 31 guaranteed the right to property as a Fundamental Right.
 
• It provided for compensation in case of acquisition or requisition of private property by the state.
 
• The article was often used to challenge land acquisition laws, delaying socio-economic reforms.
 
 
 
• **Article 300A**
 
 
• Post the 44th Amendment, the right to property was moved to Article 300A.
 
• Article 300A states that no person shall be deprived of their property save by authority of law.
 
• This made the right to property a legal right, not a Fundamental Right.
 
• It allowed the government more flexibility in implementing land reforms and socio-economic policies.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Amendment**
 
 
• The shift from a Fundamental Right to a legal right reduced the number of litigations over land acquisition.
 
• It facilitated the implementation of land reforms and equitable distribution of resources.
 
• The amendment balanced individual property rights with the need for social justice and economic development.

questions.question: In the game of Basketball, each basket shall consist of a pressure-release NBA approved metal safety ring ______ in inside diameter with a white cord net 18” in length.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**18"**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In basketball, the standard diameter of the basketball hoop is **18 inches**.
 
• The diameter of the hoop is measured from the inside edge of the rim to the opposite inside edge.
 
• This standard size is maintained in all NBA-approved games to ensure uniformity and fairness in play.
 
• The hoop is made of a pressure-release metal safety ring to enhance durability and safety during gameplay.
 
• The net attached to the hoop is **18 inches in length**, aligning with the diameter of the hoop for consistency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Basketball Backboard**

 
 
• The backboard is typically made of tempered glass, which offers a consistent rebound.
 
• The standard dimensions of a basketball backboard are 72 inches in width and 42 inches in height.
 
• The backboard provides a target for bank shots and protects the hoop from being easily damaged.
 
 
 
• **Basketball Court Dimensions**
 
 
• The standard size of a basketball court is 94 feet in length and 50 feet in width for NBA games.
 
• The free-throw line is 15 feet away from the backboard.
 
• The three-point line distance varies: 23.75 feet from the basket at the top of the key and 22 feet in the corners for NBA.
 
 
 
• **Basketball Sizes**
 
 
• A regulation basketball for men's professional play has a circumference of 29.5 inches.
 
• For women's professional play, the basketball has a circumference of 28.5 inches.
 
• Youths typically use smaller basketballs, with sizes appropriate for their age group to ensure proper handling and shooting techniques.
 
 
 
• **NBA Standards**
 
 
• The NBA specifies stringent standards for all equipment used in the game, including the hoop, backboard, and ball.
 
• These standards ensure a high level of consistency and quality in gameplay across all official matches.
 
• All equipment used must be approved by the NBA to maintain uniformity and safety for players.

questions.question: Which among the following belongs to the tertiary sector of the Indian economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Public administration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Public administration is a crucial part of the tertiary sector, which encompasses services provided by the government to its citizens.
 
• This sector includes activities like administration of public policy, maintenance of law and order, and provision of social services.
 
• Public administration plays a pivotal role in the implementation of government policies and programs.
 
• It ensures the smooth functioning of governmental operations and the delivery of public services.
 
• Public administration is vital for maintaining the welfare and security of society, making it an integral part of the tertiary sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tertiary Sector:**

 
 
• The tertiary sector, also known as the service sector, involves the provision of services rather than goods.
 
• It includes a wide range of activities such as retail, entertainment, financial services, health care, and education.
 
• This sector is crucial for economic development and is often the largest contributor to GDP in developed countries.
 
 
 
• **Economic Sectors:**
 
 
• The economy is divided into three main sectors: primary (agriculture, forestry, fishing), secondary (manufacturing, construction), and tertiary (services).
 
• Each sector plays a unique role in the economy, contributing to overall growth and development.
 
 
 
• **Public Administration Functions:**
 
 
• Public administration involves policy formulation, implementation, and the management of public programs.
 
• It also includes activities like budgeting, human resource management, and public relations.
 
 
 
• **Role in Society:**
 
 
• Public administration ensures the effective delivery of public services such as healthcare, education, and welfare programs.
 
• It also plays a crucial role in maintaining law and order and promoting social justice.

questions.question: 'Natyashashtra', the earliest text dealing with performing arts (dances and music), was compiled by which sage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Natyashastra' is an ancient Indian treatise on the performing arts, encompassing theatre, dance, and music.
 
• It was written by the sage Bharata Muni, who is regarded as the father of Indian theatrical art forms.
 
• The text is believed to have been composed between 200 BCE and 200 CE.
 
• 'Natyashastra' consists of 36 chapters with a total of 6000 shlokas (verses).
 
• It provides a detailed description of various aspects of stage performance, including music, dance, stage design, and the art of acting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharata Muni:** He is considered one of the pioneers in the field of dramatics and performing arts in India.
 
• **Rasa Theory:** The 'Natyashastra' introduces the concept of 'Rasa,' which refers to the emotional essence or flavor that the audience experiences during a performance.
 
• **Eight Rasas:** The text identifies eight primary Rasas: Shringara (love), Hasya (laughter), Karuna (sorrow), Raudra (anger), Veera (heroism), Bhayanaka (fear), Bibhatsa (disgust), and Adbhuta (wonder).
 
• **Dance Forms:** The 'Natyashastra' outlines the classical dance forms of Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, Odissi, and others.
 
• **Significance:** The 'Natyashastra' is a foundational text for classical Indian dance and theatre, influencing various art forms and cultural practices in India.

questions.question: Which of the following is the saltiest water body bordering Jordan in the east and Israel in the west?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dead Sea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Dead Sea is a salt lake bordered by Jordan to the east and Israel and Palestine to the west.
 
• It is one of the world’s saltiest bodies of water, with a salinity of 34.2%, which is almost ten times saltier than the ocean.
 
• The high salinity of the Dead Sea makes it a harsh environment for plants and animals, hence its name.
 
• It is located at the lowest point on Earth's surface on dry land, approximately 430 meters below sea level.
 
• The Dead Sea is renowned for its mineral-rich waters and therapeutic properties, attracting visitors for wellness and spa treatments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Salinity:** The Dead Sea's salinity levels are so high that it allows people to float effortlessly on the surface.
 
• **Geographical Significance:** The Dead Sea is located in the Jordan Rift Valley, and its main tributary is the Jordan River.
 
• **Historical Importance:** The region around the Dead Sea has been inhabited since prehistoric times and is referenced in various historical and religious texts.
 
• **Mineral Extraction:** The Dead Sea is a rich source of minerals such as magnesium, potassium, and bromine, which are extracted for various industrial and medicinal purposes.
 
• **Environmental Concerns:** The Dead Sea is receding at an alarming rate due to diversion of incoming water from the Jordan River and mineral extraction activities, posing significant environmental concerns.

questions.question: Who was the most famous Shaka ruler known for his inscription at Girnar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rudradaman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rudradaman I was a prominent Shaka ruler who ruled over the Western Kshatrapas.
 
• His reign is noted for the famous Junagadh rock inscription at Girnar, which is a significant historical source.
 
• The inscription, written in Sanskrit, details his achievements and the repairs he made to the Sudarshana Lake.
 
• Rudradaman's rule marked the peak of the Western Kshatrapas' power and influence in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• He is considered one of the greatest rulers of the Western Kshatrapas due to his patronage of culture and art.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Junagadh Rock Inscription**

 
 
• It is one of the oldest surviving rock inscriptions in India, dating back to 150 AD.
 
• The inscription is crucial for understanding the history of the Western Kshatrapas and the socio-political conditions of the time.
 
 
 
• **Western Kshatrapas**
 
 
• They were a dynasty of Saka rulers who controlled parts of western and central India from the 1st to the 4th centuries AD.
 
• Their rule is noted for significant contributions to trade, culture, and art.
 
 
 
• **Sudarshana Lake**
 
 
• Originally constructed during the Mauryan Empire, it was an essential irrigation project in ancient India.
 
• Rudradaman's inscription details the repairs and renovations he commissioned for the lake.
 
 
 
• **Sanskrit Inscriptions**
 
 
• Sanskrit was the classical language used in many inscriptions across ancient India, reflecting the cultural and educational priorities of the rulers.
 
• Rudradaman's use of Sanskrit in his inscriptions highlights his patronage of classical Indian culture.

questions.question: Who among the following launched the nationwide programme of Fit India Freedom Run 2.0?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anurag Thakur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Union Minister Anurag Thakur launched the Fit India Freedom Run 2.0 on August 13, 2021.
 
• The event was launched to commemorate the 75th Independence Day of India.
 
• The Fit India Freedom Run 2.0 is part of the Fit India Movement, which aims to promote fitness and health among Indians.
 
• The run covers a distance of 7.5 km, symbolizing 75 years of India's independence.
 
• It encourages citizens to participate in physical activities and stay healthy amidst the COVID-19 pandemic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fit India Movement**

 
 
• Launched by PM Narendra Modi on August 29, 2019, to encourage Indians to include physical activity and sports in their everyday lives.
 
• Aims to inspire people to adopt a fit and healthy lifestyle.
 
• Various programs and initiatives are organized under this movement to promote fitness.
 
 
 
• **Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav**
 
 
• It is an initiative by the Government of India to celebrate and commemorate 75 years of independence.
 
• It was launched on March 12, 2021, by PM Narendra Modi.
 
• Includes various events and activities to honor the freedom fighters and their contributions to India's independence.
 
 
 
• **National Sports Day**
 
 
• Celebrated on August 29 each year to honor the birth anniversary of hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand.
 
• On this day, the President of India honors eminent sports personalities with various awards.
 
• Aims to promote sports and physical activities across the country.
 
 
 
• **COVID-19 and Physical Activity**
 
 
• Regular physical activity is crucial for maintaining health during the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• It helps in boosting the immune system and reducing stress and anxiety.
 
• Various online fitness programs and challenges have been introduced to keep people active while maintaining social distancing.
